missing_examples.meaning: For infant photographs, the guiding standard is to achieve the best likeness that can reasonably be obtained given the challenges infants pose.
missing_examples.rationale: The overarching standard that 'Infants pose a particular challenge. The goal is the best likeness that can reasonably be obtained' was included in draft context quotes but was not formulated into a claim.

missing_examples.meaning: Even when a Certificate of Citizenship or Naturalization was issued recently, USCIS processing times mean that the photograph appearing on it may not satisfy the requirement of being taken within six months of passport application submission.
missing_examples.rationale: The note regarding re-use of photographs from Certificates of Naturalization or Citizenship and USCIS processing times has no counterpart claim in the draft.

missing_examples.meaning: Applicants who have physical or mental disabilities, including muscle control loss from conditions like age-related degeneration or Bell's Palsy, might be unable to display a natural or unexaggerated facial expression.
missing_examples.rationale: The informational statement regarding applicants with disabilities being unable to produce natural expressions is incorporated only as background scope in C0024 and lacks a standalone claim.

claim_results.rationale: The claim accurately captures the rule permitting infants' (especially newborns') eyes to be partially or completely closed in passport photographs. All fields are aligned with the source text and governing scope.

source_spans.quote: It is acceptable if the infant's eyes, particularly a newborn's, are partially or completely closed;

claim_results.rationale: The claim accurately reflects that discreet head support for infants is permitted, including the illustrative example of using a car seat with a white or off-white blanket.

source_spans.quote: The infant's head may be discreetly supported, e.g., a car seat with a white or off-white blanket behind the child.

claim_results.rationale: The claim accurately states that head tilt is acceptable in infant passport photographs.

source_spans.quote: Head tilt is acceptable for infants;

claim_results.rationale: The claim represents the prohibition against a parent's face appearing in the photograph of an infant.

source_spans.quote: A parent’s face cannot be in the photograph of the infant.

claim_results.rationale: The claim correctly reflects the adjudicator mandate to request a new photograph when the submitted photograph does not meet the requirements.

source_spans.quote: You must request a new photograph if the photograph submitted does not meet the following requirements:

claim_results.rationale: The claim correctly captures the requirement that the passport photograph must be in color.

source_spans.quote: The photograph must be in color;

claim_results.rationale: The claim accurately captures the recommendation/standard that the photo should be taken within six months, be a good likeness, and satisfactorily identify the applicant.

source_spans.quote: The photograph should be taken within six months of submitting the application, be a good likeness of and satisfactorily identify the applicant at the time of the application (see 22 CFR 51.26).

claim_results.rationale: The claim correctly captures the permission for hairstyles/facial hair changes relative to the ID document provided the photo remains a good likeness.

source_spans.quote: A photograph showing a change in hairstyle or facial hair from the identification document submitted is acceptable if it still is a good likeness of the applicant;

claim_results.rationale: The claim correctly captures the requirement that the photograph must be free of material damage.

source_spans.quote: The photograph must be free of material damage:

claim_results.rationale: The claim correctly reflects the definition of material damage, including its two alternative triggers (impairing likeness or impeding facial recognition).

source_spans.quote: Material damage is any damage to the facial area that makes the photograph no longer a good likeness of the applicant (e.g., creases, large holes, and large smudges) or impedes the functioning of facial recognition (damage in the area of the eyes);

claim_results.rationale: The claim accurately captures the definition of immaterial damage covering background damage and non-material facial damage.

source_spans.quote: Immaterial damage is any damage to the background, and non-material damage to the facial area (e.g., staple holes).

claim_results.rationale: The claim accurately states that immaterial damage is acceptable.

source_spans.quote: Immaterial damage is acceptable;

claim_results.rationale: The claim correctly states that the applicant does not need to sign the photograph.

source_spans.quote: The applicant does not need to sign the photograph, as this often causes creases or smudges;

claim_results.rationale: The claim accurately captures the requirement that acceptance agents sign the back of the photograph for hand-carry applications.

source_spans.quote: For hand-carry applications, the acceptance agent signs the back of the photograph.

claim_results.rationale: The claim accurately conveys that an application may be returned to adjudication to request a new photograph if a printing defect is found.

source_spans.quote: A photograph that appears acceptable and undamaged in the system may have a defect that is apparent when the passport is printed. Consequently, the passport application may be returned to adjudication to request a new photograph even though the photograph appeared acceptable.

claim_results.rationale: The claim accurately states the prohibition against eyeglasses unless they cannot be removed for medical reasons.

source_spans.quote: Eyeglasses are not acceptable unless they cannot be removed for medical reasons, e.g., the applicant has recently had ocular surgery and the eyeglasses are necessary to protect the applicant’s eyes.

claim_results.rationale: The claim accurately identifies the requirement to request a medical statement signed by a medical professional or health practitioner when eyeglasses cannot be removed for medical reasons.

source_spans.quote: A medical statement signed by a medical professional/health practitioner must be requested in these rare circumstances.

claim_results.rationale: The claim accurately reflects the prohibition that frames must not cover the eye(s) when eyeglasses are accepted for medical reasons.

source_spans.quote: If the eyeglasses are accepted for medical reasons:
The frames of the eyeglasses must not cover the eye(s);

claim_results.rationale: The claim accurately conveys that glare obscuring the eye(s) is prohibited when eyeglasses are medically accepted.

source_spans.quote: If the eyeglasses are accepted for medical reasons:
There must not be glare on eyeglasses that obscures the eye(s);

claim_results.rationale: The claim accurately represents the prohibition against shadows or refraction from eyeglasses obscuring the eye(s).

source_spans.quote: If the eyeglasses are accepted for medical reasons:
There must not be shadows or refraction from the eyeglasses that obscure the eye(s); and

claim_results.rationale: The claim accurately reflects that dark or tinted lenses are permitted if the medical statement indicates they are required.

source_spans.quote: If the eyeglasses are accepted for medical reasons:
Dark or tinted lenses are permitted if the medical statement also indicates that they are required.

claim_results.rationale: C0021 matches the source note recommending endorsement 46 limited-validity passports for temporary medical eyeglasses needs and urgent travel.

source_spans.quote: A limited-validity passport using endorsement 46 should be issued when the medical circumstance that requires eyeglasses is temporary and the applicant has urgent or emergency travel.

claim_results.rationale: C0022 accurately conveys the requirement that the applicant's expression should be natural.

source_spans.quote: The applicant’s expression should be natural.

claim_results.rationale: C0023 accurately captures the acceptability of normal unexaggerated smiles alongside the non-acceptability of unusual expressions and squinting.

source_spans.quote: Normal, unexaggerated smiles are acceptable, but unusual expressions and squinting are not.

claim_results.rationale: C0024 correctly specifies that an adjudicator may accept photographs without a natural or unexaggerated expression in qualifying disability circumstances.

source_spans.quote: You may accept a photograph without a natural or unexaggerated expression in these circumstances.

claim_results.rationale: C0025 correctly states that both eyes should be visible and open in the photo, acknowledging the infant exception.

source_spans.quote: Both of the applicant’s eyes should also be visible and open in the photograph (see the exception for infants in 8 FAM 402.1-1).

claim_results.rationale: C0026 correctly conveys permission to accept a photograph when the applicant cannot open one or both eyes due to a medical condition.

source_spans.quote: If the applicant is unable to open one or both eyes because of a medical condition, you may accept the photograph.

claim_results.rationale: C0027 accurately reflects the recommendation to request a signed medical statement in rare cases where non-conforming eyes/expressions are unlikely to be medical.

source_spans.quote: In rare cases, if it is unlikely that the closed eye(s) or exaggerated expression are because of a medical condition, you should request a medical statement signed by a medical professional/health practitioner.

claim_results.rationale: C0028 correctly details the procedure for processing and communications/customer service personnel or consular section staff regarding applications received without photographs.

source_spans.quote: Processing and communications/customer service personnel at passport agencies/centers or consular section personnel should refer applications without photographs to their supervisor for guidance on processing passport applications received without photographs;

claim_results.rationale: C0029 correctly captures the prohibition on accepting Form DS-11 or DS-82 at the public counter without a photograph.

source_spans.quote: You must not accept a form DS-11 or form DS-82 received without a photograph at the public counter.

claim_results.rationale: C0030 accurately conveys the mandate to suspend a Form DS-11 received without a photo from an acceptance facility.

source_spans.quote: Passport specialists must suspend a form DS-11 received without a photograph from an acceptance facility.

claim_results.rationale: C0031 accurately represents the requirement that the applicant must re-execute the Form DS-11.

source_spans.quote: The applicant must re-execute the form DS-11 (see IRL 975-04);

claim_results.rationale: C0032 accurately represents the requirement that specialists suspend Form DS-82 or DS-5504 received without a photograph.

source_spans.quote: Passport specialists must suspend a form DS-82 or form DS-5504 received without a photograph (see IRL 1000-05 and IRL 1018-14).
